findings.defect: The pointee fence is TYPE-based, and Go pointer conversions change the pointee type without changing the address. An own defined type over a foreign type (type L time.Location, package or function scope) makes (*L)(time.UTC) legal; a write through it is then an own named pointee and is accepted. The same holds for *x509.Certificate -> *C, &foreignField -> *ownInt, and Go 1.17 slice-to-array-pointer conversion to an own named array. This bypasses the exact promised PL-R1b property 'foreign pointee writes are refused even through a local pointer, helper parameter or an allowed pure call' for the same process-global utcLoc object as escape E2. It is not the declared storage-provenance limit: no alias or heap analysis is needed, only the type the gate already reads.
